title: Capstone: A System End to End

questions.prompt: Which may the CheckOutBook interactor depend on? Select all that apply.

options.text: The output port (an interface it owns)

questions.explanation: The interactor depends only inward — on entities and interfaces it owns (gateways, the output port). Framework request/response objects are outer details it must not import.

questions.prompt: Where are the concrete adapters (SQL gateways, presenter) constructed and connected?

options.text: At the composition root — the single wiring point near the entry point

questions.explanation: The composition root is the only place that names concrete classes and injects them, so swapping SQL for in-memory (or web for CLI) is a one-place change.

questions.prompt: You add a 'return a book' feature by writing new code behind the same kinds of ports, leaving check-out untouched — an example of the ______-Closed Principle.
questions.explanation: New behavior is added by adding code behind the same boundaries (open for extension), without modifying the existing check-out code (closed for modification).

questions.prompt: In a full request trace, how do control flow and source-code dependencies relate?

options.text: Control weaves outward (to the DB) and back (to the view), while every source-code dependency points inward

questions.explanation: The signature of a clean boundary: control can flow outward and back, but every source-code dependency points inward toward use cases and entities.

questions.prompt: Order the components a checkout request flows through, outside-in and back out.
questions.explanation: Control enters at the controller, runs the use case (which applies entity rules and uses gateways), then reports out through the presenter to the humble view.

questions.prompt: Match each capstone part to its Clean Architecture layer.
questions.explanation: Entities hold the rules, the interactor orchestrates, the gateway adapts to the database, and the framework/driver is the outer detail — with dependencies pointing inward throughout.
